description: Input validation accepts the JSON the contract describes (type-mapping 17.3 R6, decision D-136). Inputs arrive as JSON, so a date-time, UUID or enum field receives a string, and the module-invocation boundary MUST accept every string the contract's schema accepts — also when the module's contract comes from native types (a date-time class, a UUID class, an enum class) rather than from a JSON Schema document. R5 (no coercion) still holds for what the schema rejects. Measured before D-136: apcore-python validated a natively typed model in pydantic's strict PYTHON mode, which rejects an ISO string for a datetime field, a string for a UUID field and a plain string for an Enum field, so a contract-valid JSON call failed with SCHEMA_VALIDATION_ERROR. Modules declared with a JSON Schema document were unaffected, in all three SDKs.

fields.when: date-time (Python datetime, TypeScript Type.String({format: 'date-time'}), Rust chrono::DateTime<Utc>)
fields.request_id: UUID (Python uuid.UUID, TypeScript Type.String({format: 'uuid'}), Rust uuid::Uuid)
fields.level: enum of "low" | "high" (Python an Enum class with string values, TypeScript a union of the two literals, Rust a serde enum renamed to lowercase)

driver_contract.path: Declare the module from NATIVE types in the SDK's own idiom — as listed in `module_contract.fields`; a JSON Schema document is the path that already works and does not exercise the decision — register it with a real Executor, and call it through the public call path with `input.inputs` as parsed JSON.
driver_contract.outcome: `expected.output` is the result when the call succeeds; `expected.error_code` the wire code of the error it raises.

test_cases.description: R5 still applies: a string the schema does not accept is rejected.
The over-correction guard: switching to lax validation would accept a Unix timestamp for a date-time field. The contract says string.
